taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Bank-road, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 640 | 5.21 | 5.21
2 | 934 | 8.58 | 13.8
3 | 2594 | 84.1 | 97.9
4 | 4386 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as AA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Bank-road, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Bank-road Station, Bori Metropolis**

The VES interpretation at Bank-road resolved four layers. Layer 1 (640 Ω·m) extends to 5.21 m depth, underlain by Layer 2 (934 Ω·m) to 13.8 m, then Layer 3 (2594 Ω·m) to 97.9 m, and a resistive basement-like Layer 4 (4386 Ω·m) below. Resistivity increases monotonically with depth across all layers.

Applying the curve-type convention: layers 1-2-3 give r1 < r2 < r3 → A; layers 2-3-4 give r2 < r3 < r4 → A. This yields "AA", consistent with the on-file classification. Since all letters are identical, the curve may equivalently be expressed as a single "A" (continuous resistivity increase, typical of a simple multi-layer A-type sounding). The filed "AA-type" label is therefore an acceptable notation and matches the computed layer sequence. No discrepancy was found; drilling planning can proceed using this model.

{"curve_type_stated": "AA", "label_issue_flagged": false}
